methods.label: Compare each increase with its original population
methods.explanation:
A percentage increase compares the population gained with the population in 1970, so we divide each increase by its starting population.

Reading the two number lines, the populations in thousands change as follows: \(A:40\to50\), \(B:50\to70\), \(C:70\to100\), \(D:100\to130\), and \(E:120\to160\). The common unit of thousands cancels in every ratio. The relative increases are therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&:\frac{50-40}{40}=\frac14,\\
B&:\frac{70-50}{50}=\frac25,\\
C&:\frac{100-70}{70}=\frac37,\\
D&:\frac{130-100}{100}=\frac3{10},\\
E&:\frac{160-120}{120}=\frac13.
\end{aligned}
\]
The fractions \(1/4\), \(3/10\), and \(1/3\) are all less than \(2/5\). To compare the remaining two, use a common denominator:
\[
\frac37=\frac{15}{35}>\frac{14}{35}=\frac25.
\]
Thus city \(\boxed{C}\) has the greatest percentage increase, namely \(\frac37\cdot100\%=\frac{300}{7}\%\), about \(42.86\%\). The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
